scenario: RFCS.6a.4 / [LFAC.2.5.3]: an emit that supersedes a live fact records its FactEmit -- on the stream callback, DS_EV_FACT_ASSERT -- and then the withdrawal of the fact it superseded, whatever produced the new fact. `copy` emits `Out logical` with the constant key 1 and the Reading's v, so two Readings of different `src` emit the same Out identity. Reading src 1 (v 1) is asserted and pumped: `copy` emits Out(1, 1). Reading src 2 (v 2) is asserted and pumped: `copy` fires for it and its emit replaces Out(1, 1) with Out(1, 2) while Out(1, 1) is still justified, so no truth-maintenance retraction removes it first and the supersedure is the emit's own. (An upsert of ONE Reading cannot drive this: its old activation ends, truth maintenance retracts the old Out, and the new emit supersedes nothing.) Exactly, strict: the first clock sample's tick; the first input, its pump and firing; the second input and pump; the firing whose emit records fact_assert(Out 2) then fact_retract(Out 1) and only then its action_emit. PATH PINNED: libds's rule-emit path (rete/adapters.c adapter_ds_emit, through ds_rete_wm_wrap_emitted_fact) and Mercury's ds.exec assert_verb `replaced` arm, held to each other by the runtime differential. NOT COVERED: an `as`-keyed re-fire's supersedure ([LRST.2.2]). It is a separate sweep action (libds do_retract_corr_sweep, Mercury's ds.exec corr sweep) over a fact of another identity, and it keeps action order, its FactWithdraw ahead of the FactEmit (RFCS.6a.4, [LCRS.6.2.1]); this vector drives one-identity supersedure only.
rules_ds:
schema Reading scope logical:
    src: Int key
    v: Int mutable

schema Out scope logical:
    id: Int key
    v: Int mutable

rule copy:
    Reading r
->
    emit Out logical id: 1 v: r.v
